_about: Per-state review notes. Every note restates only what its linked source says (each source page was opened; archived text in book-audit/deep/sources/rht_states/). Quotes are verbatim. Nothing here is estimated.

notes.text: New Hampshire's program is run by the Governor's Office of New Opportunities & Rural Transformational Health (GO-NORTH), which Gov. Kelly Ayotte set up in January 2026 as an independent entity under the governor's office rather than having the Department of Health and Human Services administer the money.

GO-NORTH routes most Year 1 money through five funding hubs that have received or been allocated $161.2 million of the $204 million: Foundation for Healthy Communities (an affiliate of the New Hampshire Hospital Association) $66.5M; Community Development Finance Authority $48.3M; Community Behavioral Health Association $21.6M; University System of New Hampshire $15.7M; Community College System of New Hampshire $9.1M.

Outside the hubs: $20 million to Health Strategies – Endowment for Health; $1.7 million to NORC at the University of Chicago for independent evaluation; $14.7 million in budget lines (a “TBD Healthcare System Pilot” and two DHHS contracts) that the reporters could not explain.
GO-NORTH's director says the state has awarded more than $11 million to rural emergency medical services organizations to expand emergency services and launch Mobile Integrated Health programs.

CMS records New Hampshire as having put its entire Year 1 award to work by July 31, 2026 (state-reported obligations). The same reporting notes that the Executive Council approved the first-year distribution plan in March and that many requests for proposals were not released until October and November 2026.

quotes.q: We were among the first states in the country to have our first-year budget fully approved and obligated
This money needs to already be put to work. We’re still just releasing RFPs (request for proposals).
quotes.who: Karen Liot Hill, Executive Councilor (District 2), recalling the governor's March meeting

notes.text: In July 2026 Maine's Department of Health and Human Services released $30 million of RHT funds to 11 hospitals chosen on key financial indicators to boost financial stability: Cary Medical Center, MaineHealth Franklin Hospital, Houlton Regional Hospital, MaineGeneral Medical Center – Alfond Center for Health, Millinocket Regional Hospital, Mount Desert Island Hospital, Northern Light AR Gould Hospital, Northern Light CA Dean Hospital, Northern Maine Medical Center, MaineHealth Pen Bay Hospital and Penobscot Valley Hospital.
Participating hospitals receive technical assistance, must submit plans to the state by January 2027, and must implement projects by August 2027.

Maine's Year 2 award is roughly $350,000 more than Year 1. Year 2 priorities include more school-based health centers and mobile health units, integrating primary care into behavioral health clinics, tribal traditional healing practices, and better electronic medical records for jails.
